mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for three consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has exceeded 4.5% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and decline in the unemployment rate signals a tightening monetary policy amid a strong labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to heightened recession risks.
regime_hint: tight labor market with monetary tightening
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has risen and UNRATE has fallen over the past month, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high labor market tightness (unemployment rate below 4.0% and payroll growth above 200k), the S&P 500 tends to underperform in the following 20 trading days due to overheating concerns and potential policy tightening.
regime_hint: high labor market tightness (UNRATE < 4.0%, PAYEMS growth > 200k)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting high labor market tightness criteria, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate over the past three months indicates a tightening labor market that boosts corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE has declined for three consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1200 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals weakening consumer demand and potential economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where HOUST has fallen below 1200 for two consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production over the past three months indicates robust supply chain activity and economic expansion, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO has increased for three consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (strong GDP growth and high retail sales), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to valuation concerns and the likelihood of monetary policy tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting late-cycle expansion criteria, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
